summary: Cobalt thin films were deposited using a remote plasma ALD method with dicobalt octacarbonyl as the precursor. The study investigated the effect of plasma power on impurity content and silicide formation. The deposition rate was 1.2 Å per cycle in the ALD window of 75–110°C. Impurity content, such as oxygen and carbon, was influenced by plasma power, with higher plasma power reducing impurities. Silicide formation was observed after rapid thermal annealing.
evidence: Cobalt thin films were deposited by a remote plasma atomic layer deposition /H20849ALD/H20850system with a metalorganic precursor of dicobalt octacarbonyl /H20849Co2/H20849CO/H208508/H20850. The deposition rate of Co films was /H110111.2 Å/cycle in the ALD window of 75–110°C. The extent of impurity content such as oxygen and carbon was highly affected by plasma power. The impurity content was minimized when H2 plasma was used with a plasma power of 300 W. Silicide formation was observed after RTA.
